clue.text: Stir by subtle means

indicators.note: by subtle means suggests the letters of subtle are worked round by some method into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone stirs things up quietly, by cunning rather than force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'means' is the anagram signal: SUBTLE rearranged gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Bustle is busy activity or commotion, much like a stir.

clue.text: Rose trains and that is right

parts.note: BR, British Rail, ran the UK trains
ie, id est, means that is

explanation.surface: Someone rose to their feet, trained, and was proved right.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rose' looks like a verb but names a flower. BR was British Rail, the old UK national railway.
explanation.definitionFit: The brier, or sweet briar, is a wild shrub of the rose family.

clue.text: A painter's jacket

explanation.surface: An artist's favourite coat.
explanation.definitionFit: Stanley Spencer was an English artist, and a spencer is a short close-fitting jacket.

clue.text: Hiding brilliance is a cover-up

explanation.surface: Concealing one's talent is a form of cover-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A lampshade masks a bulb's glare and is a cover fitted over a light.

clue.text: The French examination -the final

parts.note: la is the feminine form of 'the' in French
a test is an examination

explanation.surface: A French paper sat as the last exam of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: The latest thing is the most recent, the final one so far.

clue.text: Strange article about a deliberately misleading story

indicators.note: the article goes round, about, the story

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a lie is a deliberately false account

explanation.surface: An odd news piece about a made-up tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' looks like a news item but is the grammatical article AN, round LIE.
explanation.definitionFit: Alien means foreign or unfamiliar, so odd.

clue.text: More weight to remove!

parts.note: extra means more
ct, carat, is a unit of weight for gems

explanation.surface: A dieter is urged to shed more weight.
explanation.definitionFit: To extract is to draw out, to take away.

clue.text: Fruit of Argentine origins

indicators.note: the origins, the raw material, of the answer are the letters of Argentine in another order

explanation.surface: Fruit that comes from Argentina.
explanation.definitionFit: A tangerine is a small citrus, like a mandarin orange.

clue.text: Ideal characters found accepting an honour a problem

indicators.note: the shuffled letters take in another piece, so accepting signals a container
the characters (letters) of ideal are to be found in a fresh arrangement

parts.note: MM is the Military Medal, a British honour

explanation.surface: A principled person is torn over whether to accept an award.
explanation.walkthrough: IDEAL rearranged gives DILEA, and 'accepting' puts MM (Military Medal) inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilemma is a hard choice between options, a kind of problem.

clue.text: Separating if in smart environment

indicators.note: if is placed in another word, so in marks a container
the word for smart forms the surroundings, the environment, of if

parts.note: to smart is to sting

explanation.surface: Sorting things out in a stylish setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smart' looks like an adjective (stylish) but is the verb: to smart is to STING, which surrounds IF.
explanation.definitionFit: Sifting sorts material by passing it through a sieve, separating fine from coarse.

clue.text: Many churchmen are men with businesses to rum

annotationWithheld.why: Many churchmen are men with businesses to run (9), scan confirms 'run': D (many) + RECTORS leaves an I that no clue word supplies
annotationWithheld.clue: Many churchmen are men with businesses to rum

clue.text: In favour of giving up the file

parts.note: pro means in favour of
a cession is a giving up of rights or territory

explanation.surface: Someone supports surrendering a dossier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'file' is not a dossier here but a line of people moving one behind another.
explanation.definitionFit: A procession is people moving in a line, which is what single file describes.

clue.text: A stake providing support

parts.note: a bet is a stake laid on an outcome

explanation.surface: A wager offered as backing.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet is to help or encourage, usually in wrongdoing, which is a way of giving backing.

clue.text: Country scholar after back-massage

indicators.note: the scholar comes after the reversed piece
back, joined to massage, tells us to read the word for massage backwards

parts.note: to rub is to massage
MA, Master of Arts, is a scholar

explanation.surface: A country academic turns up after a back rub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-massage' looks like a treatment for the back; 'back' turns RUB into BUR, and MA follows. Burma is the former name of Myanmar.
explanation.definitionFit: Burma is the former name of Myanmar, a nation in South-East Asia.

clue.text: The warder, a striker, keeping the price up

indicators.note: the striker holds, keeps, the price inside

parts.note: a beater is one who strikes

indicators.note: in a down clue, up says the word for the price is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: a fee is a price charged

explanation.surface: A guard and a forward combine to push prices up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses FEE to EEF, which BEATER holds. A Beefeater is a Yeoman Warder at the Tower of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Beefeaters are the ceremonial guards at the Tower of London, officially Yeoman Warders.

clue.text: A scientist bearing in a mug

parts.note: E, east, is a compass bearing
a stein is a German beer mug

explanation.surface: A scientist peers into a beer mug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearing' is a compass point, E for east, not carrying.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Einstein was the physicist behind relativity.

clue.text: Grant Iran arranged — it could be telling

indicators.note: the letters of Grant Iran are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A grant to Iran is set up, which may say a lot.
explanation.definitionFit: Narrating is recounting a story, which is what telling one means.

clue.text: Shut up about money required for a bit of building

indicators.note: the word for shut up goes round, about, the money

parts.note: pent, as in pent up, means shut up
a dime is a ten-cent coin, a piece of money

explanation.surface: Someone is told to be quiet about the cost of a building job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shut up' reads as an order to be quiet but is PENT, as in pent-up; it goes round DIME.
explanation.definitionFit: A pediment is the triangular gable over a classical portico, an architectural feature.

clue.text: Little page, framed by a crawler, making check

indicators.note: the page sits inside the crawler as in a frame

parts.note: an insect is a creeping creature
p is the short form of page

explanation.surface: A small sheet is enclosed by a creepy-crawly, prompting an inspection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crawler' suggests a toady but is an INSECT, round P.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect is to examine closely, to check.

clue.text: The weapon of a novice in general

indicators.note: the novice sits in the word for general

parts.note: rife means widespread, general
L, for learner, is a novice

explanation.surface: A raw recruit carries the general's weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'general' looks like the army rank but means widespread, RIFE, which takes in L.
explanation.definitionFit: A rifle is a long-barrelled gun, a firearm.

clue.text: Leaves gaol if set free before mid-September

indicators.note: the anagram comes before the middle letter
the letters of gaol if are released into a new order
mid- picks the central letter of September

explanation.surface: A prisoner leaves jail on release before the middle of September.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' reads as a verb but is the noun. GAOL IF rearranged gives FOLIAG, then E, the middle letter of September.
explanation.definitionFit: Foliage is the leaves of a plant as a mass.

clue.text: Hash is available in the canteen

explanation.surface: Hash is on the menu in the canteen.
explanation.definitionFit: A hash is a muddle or jumble, and a mess is also where service personnel eat together.

clue.text: Tiny flowers possibly matter less

indicators.note: possibly says the letters of matter less could form something else

explanation.surface: Little blooms might not matter much.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowers' are things that flow, not blooms; MATTER LESS rearranged gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Streamlets are small streams, so they are little things that flow.

clue.text: Taste drink with some hesitation -find it excellent

parts.note: to sup is to take a sip, taste drink
er is a hesitant noise

explanation.surface: Someone sips a drink hesitantly and finds it wonderful.
explanation.definitionFit: Super is informal for first-rate.

clue.text: Bearers of 19 down in the centre establishing their claim

indicators.note: the run of letters sits in the words centre establishing

explanation.surface: Those bearing leaves stake out their claim in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: '19 down' refers to the clue for FOLIAGE, so the definition means bearers of leaves; 'in' signals the run hidden across the words.
explanation.definitionFit: Trees carry leaves, being what grows them.

clue.text: Try a little meat temptingly presented

indicators.note: only a little of the words meat temptingly is taken, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Have a taste of some temptingly served meat.
explanation.definitionFit: An attempt is an effort, a go, which is what a try is.

clue.text: The drop-out appearing in black and white will be copied

indicators.note: the drop-out turns up inside the word for black and white

parts.note: pied means patched black and white, like a magpie
a rat is one who deserts, drops out

explanation.surface: A drop-out featured in print will find their work reproduced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'black and white' suggests print but is PIED; RAT, a deserter, goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Pirated means reproduced without permission, so copied illegally.

clue.text: Official report about a new tendency

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a turn is a new development or tendency, as in events taking a turn

explanation.surface: An official write-up on a new trend.
explanation.definitionFit: A return is a formal statement filed with an authority, such as a tax form.

clue.text: Monstrous female Greek absorbed in love letter

indicators.note: the Greek is taken inside the other pieces

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O
ess is the name of the letter S

explanation.surface: A Greek woman is engrossed in a love letter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love letter' looks like a romantic note but is O (zero) and ESS (the letter S), with GR inside.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogress is a female giant of folk tales, a monster.
